statement: The production admin CDC surface owns exactly one live SystemTableCache notification subscription: construction and repeated same-cache binding never duplicate delivery, cache handoff prevents the retired cache from delivering while the replacement remains live, shutdown detaches delivery, and the unchanged release-blocking admin CDC integration passes repeatedly under the release environment without timeout or listener leakage; cache mutation, tombstone fencing, CDC operation payloads, and non-admin subscribers remain unchanged.

constraints.statement: Treat the release failure as an observer-lifecycle boundary problem until cache mutation, listener scheduling, admin subscription ownership, initialization, handoff, shutdown, test teardown, and release-runner behavior have been traced together; do not patch one missed assertion locally.

AdminWebSocketAPI owns one stable cache listener and one explicit bind/unbind lifecycle. Rebinding the same cache is idempotent, replacing a cache detaches the prior cache first, and shutdown releases the subscription.
Do not raise timeouts, add sleeps, weaken assertions, skip or quarantine the integration, reduce release proof, or change runner retry/concurrency policy to make the witness green.
Do not weaken SystemTableCache tombstone fencing, mutation ordering, asynchronous listener isolation, CDC table classification, or error isolation for other subscribers.
The regression must exercise the production AdminWebSocketAPI and SystemTableCache path, prove repeated lifecycle plateau and stale-cache non-delivery, and fail when the ownership repair is reverted.
After the last source-changing attempt and before landing, obtain category-complete independent lifecycle, owner-boundary, and harness-fidelity verification and record it through Solver.
The immutable v0.2.0 tag is never moved or deleted. If source bytes change, publish the exact landed head and cut the next 0.2 patch release only after exact-SHA CI and release preflight pass.
